In what year was Indira Gandhi born?
Indira Gandhi: During her father Jawaharlal Nehru's premiership from 1947 to 1964, Gandhi was his hostess and accompanied him on his numerous foreign trips.
In what year was Edward VII born?
Edward VII: As Prince of Wales, Edward travelled throughout Britain performing ceremonial public duties and represented Britain on visits abroad.
In what year was Charles III born?
Charles III (Charles Philip Arthur George; born 14 November 1948) is King of the United Kingdom and the 14 other Commonwealth realms.
In what year was Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh born?
Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh: Philip was born in Greece into the Greek and Danish royal families.
In what year did Empress Elisabeth of Austria die?
Empress Elisabeth of Austria: Elisabeth was born into the Bavarian House of Wittelsbach but enjoyed an informal upbringing before marrying her first cousin, Emperor Franz Joseph I, at 16.
In what year did Golda Meir die?
Golda Meir (previously Meyerson; née Mabovitch; 3 May 1898 – 8 December 1978) was the prime minister of Israel from 1969 to 1974.
In what year did Qasem Soleimani die?
Qasem Soleimani: Former Mossad director Yossi Cohen said Soleimani's strategies had "personally tightened a noose around Israel's neck".
In what year was People's Party (Spain) founded?
People's Party (Spain): The People's Party was a 1989 re-foundation of People's Alliance (AP), a party led by former minister Manuel Fraga.
In what year was Timurid Empire founded?
Timurid Empire: The empire led to the Timurid Renaissance, particularly during the reign of astronomer and mathematician Ulugh Begh.
Rashidun Caliphate: Abu Bakr. The title Rashidun stems from the doctrine in Sunni Islam that the caliphs were "rightly guided".
Pahlavi dynasty: Reza Shah. The rest of the country was taken by 1923, and by October 1925 the Majlis agreed to depose and formally exile Ahmad Shah Qajar.
House of Habsburg: Guntram the Rich. The house takes its name from Habsburg Castle, a fortress built in the 1020s in present-day Switzerland by Radbot of Klettgau, who named his fortress Habsburg.
In which country is House of Tudor?
House of Tudor: Kingdom of England. The House of Tudor (TEW-dər) was an English and Welsh dynasty that held the throne of England from 1485 to 1603.
In which country is Second Chechen War?
Second Chechen War: Russia. Russian authorities were quick to blame Chechens for the bombings, although no Chechen, field commander or otherwise, took responsibility for the attacks.
In which country is Burning Man?
Burning Man: United States. Burning Man is a week-long large-scale desert event focused on "community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance" held annually in the Western United States.
In which country is Battle of Ilovaisk?
Battle of Ilovaisk: Ukraine. The Russian side opened fire on the evacuating Ukrainian soldiers, many of whom died whilst trying to escape.
In which country is Avignon Papacy?
Avignon Papacy: France. Clement refused to move to Rome, and in 1309 he moved his court to the papal enclave at Avignon, where it remained for the next 67 years.
In which country is History of New South Wales?

History of New South Wales: Australia. The history of New South Wales refers to the history of the Australian state of New South Wales and the area's preceding Indigenous and British colonial societies.
In which country did the Battle of Bunker Hill take place?
Battle of Bunker Hill: Thirteen Colonies. The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought on June 17, 1775, during the Siege of Boston in the first stage of the American Revolutionary War.
In which country did the Siege of Osaka take place?
Siege of Osaka: Japan. The siege put an end to the last major armed opposition to the establishment of the Tokugawa shogunate.
In which country is Yesh Atid based?
Yesh Atid: Israel. Yesh Atid (Hebrew: יֵשׁ עָתִיד, lit. 'There is a Future') is a centrist political party in Israel.
In which country is Battle of Warsaw (1920) based?
Battle of Warsaw (1920): Poland. After the Polish Kiev offensive, Soviet forces launched a successful counterattack in summer 1920, forcing the Polish army to retreat westward.
Which of these was an official language of the Byzantine Empire?
Byzantine Empire: medieval Latin. The term 'Byzantine Empire' was coined only after its demise; its citizens used the term 'Roman Empire' and called themselves 'Romans'.
Which of these was an official language of Great Moravia?
Great Moravia: Old Church Slavonic. The formations preceding it in these territories were Samo's tribal union (631–658) and the Pannonian Avar state (567–822).
Which of these was an official language of Bahmani Kingdom?
Bahmani Kingdom: Persian. The Bahmani Kingdom, or the Bahmani Sultanate, was a late medieval Persianate kingdom that ruled the Deccan Plateau in India.
Who is credited with discovering Permaculture?
Permaculture: Bill Mollison. Permaculture is an approach to land management and settlement design that adopts arrangements observed in flourishing natural ecosystems.

This political movement to end slavery gained major momentum in the western world during the late 1700s and 1800s, though France had briefly outlawed the practice as early as 1315 — what movement is it?
Abolitionism is the political movement to end slavery and liberate enslaved individuals around the world.

This Russian politician served as personal bodyguard to President Putin before rising to lead special forces that oversaw the 2014 annexation of Crimea, later becoming Deputy Defense Minister — who is he?
Aleksey Dyumin (born 28 August 1972) is a Russian politician serving as Secretary of the State Council since 2024.
Often called "The Father of the Philippine Revolution," this Filipino hero co-founded and led the secret society known as the Katipunan in its fight against Spanish colonial rule — who was he?
Andrés Bonifacio (November 30, 1863 - May 10, 1897) was a Filipino revolutionary leader.
Rising through Chile's army to General Chief of Staff, this officer toppled an elected president in 1973 and ran a military dictatorship for 17 years — who was he?
Augusto Pinochet (25 November 1915 - 10 December 2006) was a Chilean army officer and military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990.
Nicknamed 'Bibi,' this MIT graduate and former Sayeret Matkal commando became his country's longest-serving prime minister. Who is he?
Benjamin Netanyahu (born 21 October 1949), nicknamed "Bibi", is an Israeli politician and diplomat who has served as Prime Minister of Israel since 2022.
A Methodist minister and theologian, he became Zimbabwe's first, ceremonial head of state in 1980 before Robert Mugabe succeeded him as executive president — who was he?
Canaan Banana (5 March 1936 - 10 November 2003) was a Zimbabwean Methodist minister, theologian, and politician who served as the first President of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 1987.
A U.S. senator from New York since 1999, this Democratic politician has led his party's Senate caucus since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader at different points — who is he?
Chuck Schumer (born November 23, 1950) is an American politician serving since 1999 as a United States senator from New York.

Iceland's longest-serving prime minister, this former mayor of Reykjavík later chaired the Central Bank — only to face loud public demands for his resignation amid the 2008 financial crisis. Who was he?
Davíð Oddsson (17 January 1948 - 1 March 2026) was an Icelandic politician, and the longest-serving prime minister of Iceland, in office from 1991 to 2004.
Followers of this modern movement pick careers and donate to charities based on rigorous cost-benefit calculations, aiming to maximize positive impact worldwide — what movement is this?
Effective altruism (EA) is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good.
On 30 April 1975, North Vietnamese forces under General Van Tien Dung captured South Vietnam's capital, triggering a frantic evacuation and ending the Vietnam War — what is this event called?

Fall of Saigon was captured by North Vietnam on 30 April 1975. The aftermath ushered in a transition period under the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam until the formal reunification in 1976.

This Indonesian politician governed Central Java for a decade before finishing third in the 2024 presidential race, having earlier spent two terms as a national legislator representing the same province — who is he?
Ganjar Pranowo (born 28 October 1968) is an Indonesian politician who served as the governor of Central Java between 2013 and 2023.

This Russian mystic and faith healer gained enormous influence over the imperial family of Tsar Nicholas II in the final years of the empire. Born a Siberian peasant in 1869, he's best remembered for his mysterious sway over the fate of Russia itself — who is this controversial figure?
Grigori Rasputin was Russian mystic (1869–1916). Grigori Yefimovich Rasputin (21 January [O.S. 9 January] 1869 – 30 December [O.S. 17 December] 1916) was a Russian mystic and faith healer.
Mother of two future English kings, this queen consort fled to her home country during the English Civil War in 1644, only to be left impoverished after her husband's execution — who is she?
Henrietta Maria of France (25 November 1609 - 10 September 1669) was Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland from her marriage to King Charles I on 13 June 1625 until his execution on 30 January 1649.
After serving as the 29th chief of Turkey's General Staff, this general won a parliamentary seat for Kayseri in 2023 — who is he?
Hulusi Akar (born 12 March 1952) is a retired four-star Turkish Armed Forces general who served as the Minister of National Defense from 2018 to 2023.
The eldest son of a former U.S. president and first lady, this businessman and environmentalist ran as the Democratic nominee in Nevada's 2006 Senate election — who is he?
Jack Carter (politician) (born July 3, 1947) is an American businessman, politician and environmentalist.
This biblical queen, wife of King Ahab of Israel, was thrown from a window on the orders of Jehu and devoured by dogs, as the prophet Elijah had foretold — who was she?
Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible (1 Kings 16).
Born in Wales and raised in Adelaide, this Labor politician became the first and only woman to serve as both deputy prime minister and prime minister of Australia — who is she?
Julia Gillard (born 29 September 1961) is an Australian former politician who served as the 27th prime minister of Australia from 2010 to 2013.
Founded around 1399 in southern India, this geopolitical realm eventually became a British princely state from 1799 to 1947, persisting until 1950. What was it?
Kingdom of Mysore was a geopolitical realm in southern India founded in around 1399 in the vicinity of the modern-day city of Mysuru and prevailed until 1950.
This Chinese aerospace engineer spent 31 years at a satellite launch center before becoming his country's Minister of National Defense for just seven months in 2023 — who is he?
Li Shangfu (pinyin: L Shngf; born February 1958) is a Chinese aerospace engineer and former military administrator.
The Sanskrit word for 'human' literally means 'child of' this figure, an archetypal first man in Hindu tradition also considered the progenitor of humanity — who is he?
Manu (Hinduism) is a term found with various meanings in Hinduism.

This civil rights activist became the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi, working to desegregate the University of Mississippi and expand Black voting rights before his 1963 assassination — who was he?
Medgar Evers (July 2, 1925 - June 12, 1963) was an American civil rights activist who was the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi.
The final ruler of Iran until 1979, he took the title 'King of Kings' in 1967 and held others including 'Light of the Aryans.' Who was he?
Mohammad Reza Pahlavi (26 October 1919 - 27 July 1980) was the last Shah of Iran from 1941 to 1979.

Launched in 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman at the northern tip of the Red Sea, this 26,500-square-kilometer megaproject was widely mocked as unrealistic before being scaled way back. What is it?
Neom is a megaproject in Tabuk Province in Saudi Arabia.
A member of the Bundestag since 2006 representing Hesse, this German-Iranian politician co-led Alliance 90/The Greens with Ricarda Lang and now serves as Vice President of the Bundestag — who is he?
Omid Nouripour (born 18 June 1975) is a German-Iranian politician who has been serving as Vice President of the Bundestag since 2025.
This Finnish politician has led his country's National Coalition Party since 2016, and became prime minister of Finland in 2023 after previously serving as finance minister — who is he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Petteri Orpo (born 3 November 1969) is a Finnish politician currently serving as the prime minister of Finland since 2023.
A democratic socialist economist, this Ecuadorian served as his country's 45th president from 2007 to 2017 and has lived in Belgium since leaving office — who is he?
Rafael Correa (Spanish; born 6 April 1963) is an Ecuadorian politician and economist who served as the 45th president of Ecuador from 2007 to 2017.
First elected to a European legislature in 2013, this Maltese politician rose to become the first female president of that body since 2002 — who is she?
Roberta Metsola (ne Tedesco Triccas; born 18 January 1979) is a Maltese politician who has served as the president of the European Parliament since January 2022.
This Turkmen leader gave himself the title 'Türkmenbaşy' — Leader of all Turkmen — and ruled from the Soviet era until his death in 2006; who was he?
Saparmurat Niyazov (19 February 1940 - 21 December 2006) was a Turkmen politician and dictator who led Turkmenistan from 1985 until his death in 2006.
This Indian actress won acclaim for playing Tulsi Virani in a hit soap opera before pivoting to politics as a Bharatiya Janata Party leader who has held several Union Cabinet posts — who is she?
Smriti Irani (ne Malhotra; born 23 March 1976) is an Indian actress, politician, fashion model, and television producer.
This American politician has served as junior U.S. senator from Texas since 2013, after earlier serving as the state's solicitor general and later chairing the Senate Commerce Committee — who is he?
Ted Cruz (born December 22, 1970) is an American politician and attorney serving as the junior United States senator from Texas since 2013.

Tracing its roots to Radical Protestantism and Restorationism, this creedless faith tradition blends influences from Buddhism, Hinduism, Judaism and beyond under shared covenants of love — which tradition is this?
Unitarian Universalism (UUism or UU) is a liberal religious tradition characterized by its commitment to theological diversity, inclusivity, and social justice.

Married to Puyi, the last emperor of China, in 1922, this Manchu noblewoman later became empress consort of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo from 1934 until its monarchy was abolished in 1945 — name this empress?
Wanrong (13 November 1906 - 20 June 1946), of the Manchu Plain White Banner Gobulo clan, was the wife and empress consort of Puyi, the last emperor of China.
This Korean admiral is remembered for winning every one of at least 23 naval battles he fought against the Japanese navy during a 16th-century war — who was he?
Yi Sun-sin (Korean; April 28, 1545 - December 16, 1598) was a Korean admiral and military general known for his victories against the Japanese navy during the Imjin War in the Joseon period.
As head of the presidential guard, this officer overthrew Niger's president in a 2023 coup and was formally inaugurated as president two years later. Who is he?
Abdourahamane Tchiani: President of Niger since 2025.
Nearly blind and a quadriplegic reliant on a wheelchair after a teenage sporting accident, this imam founded and led an Islamist organization until his 2004 assassination — who was he?
Ahmed Yassin: Palestinian political and religious leader (1936–2004)
His simultaneous election as Prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia in 1859 effectively united the two states — making which liberal reformer the first domnitor of the Romanian Principalities?
Alexandru Ioan Cuza: First ruler of the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (1820–1873)

Mentioned on the Merneptah Stele around 1208 BCE, these two neighboring Iron Age kingdoms in the Southern Levant were said to have once been united under kings Saul, David, and Solomon — what are they?
Ancient Israel and Judah: Near Eastern civilization during the Iron Age.
Son of Zeus and Hera and brother to strategy-minded Athena, which Olympian embodied war's raw brutality and bloodlust rather than tactics?
Ares: God of war in ancient Greek religion.

A Sunni Muslim Kurdish dynasty that founded the medieval Sultanate of Egypt in 1171 under Saladin, who abolished the Fatimid Caliphate after originally serving the Zengid ruler Nur al-Din. What dynasty was this?
Ayyubid dynasty: Sultanate in Egypt and Levant from 1171 to 1341.

This Ottoman sultan ruled from 1481 to 1512, welcomed Sephardi Jews expelled from Spain following the 1492 Alhambra Decree, and eventually abdicated his throne to his son, Selim I. Which sultan is this?
Bayezid II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512. Bayezid; 3 December 1447/1448 – 26 May 1512) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512.
This accountant-turned-politician served as governor of Lagos State before becoming Nigeria's 16th president in 2023, having earlier gone into exile under military ruler Sani Abacha — who is he?
Bola Tinubu: President of Nigeria since 2023. Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Adekunle Tinubu (born 29 March 1952) is a Nigerian politician serving as the 16th and current president of Nigeria since 2023.

This German jurist joined the Nazi Party in 1933 and used his legal theories to provide ideological justification for the regime, though he fell out of favor with senior officials by 1936 — who is he?
Carl Schmitt: German jurist and political theorist (1888–1985)
Born into a German duchy and married to King George III, this queen served an astonishing 57 years as Britain's longest-serving queen consort and also became Queen of Hanover. Who was she?
Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz: Queen of Great Britain and Ireland from 1761 to 1818.

Daniel Noboa: President of Ecuador since 2023. Before his political career, Noboa served in several positions at Noboa Corporation, an exporting business founded by his grandfather.
The first woman to become president of Peru, she took office in December 2022 after her predecessor's failed attempt to dissolve Congress, and was herself removed from power in 2025 — who is she?
Dina Boluarte: President of Peru from 2022 to 2025. Boluarte aligned herself with the right-wing majority of the Peruvian Congress, and received support from the Peruvian Armed Forces.
Alongside Tenzing Norgay, this New Zealand mountaineer became one of the first two people confirmed to reach the top of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953 — who is he?
Selected in 1866 to marry the future King Gojong, this consort — known in her lifetime as Queen Min — saw her own clan push the regent, her father-in-law, out of power. Who was she?
Empress Myeongseong: Regent of Joseon from 1873 to 1895.
Aided by his interpreter La Malinche and thousands of Tlaxcaltec allies, Hernán Cortés ended the Aztec civilization with this 1521 siege — what's the event called?
Fall of Tenochtitlan: 1521 conquest of the Aztec capital by the Spanish Empire and rival indigenous tribes.

Sparked partly by the 'Ems dispatch' after a Hohenzollern prince's bid for the Spanish throne collapsed, this 1870-71 conflict pitted France against a German confederation led by Otto von Bismarck — which conflict?

Rising to prominence during Greece's government-debt crisis, this far-right, neo-Nazi organization became the third-largest party in the Greek parliament following the January 2015 election, before its support collapsed — which group?
Golden Dawn (Greece): Greek neo-Nazi criminal organisation.
Serving as both his country's first prime minister and later its third president, this Namibian leader also chaired the Southern African Development Community starting in 2018 — who is he?
Hage Geingob: President of Namibia from 2015 to 2024.
Said to be a daughter of Loki, this Norse underworld ruler was appointed by Odin to preside over a shadowy realm in Niflheim, where she receives a portion of the dead — who is she?
Hel (mythological being): Underworld entity in Norse mythology.

This German banker headed the Reichsbank in both the Weimar Republic and the early Nazi era, and helped persuade Hindenburg to appoint Hitler's first government despite later opposing some rearmament policies — who is he?
Hjalmar Schacht: German politician, banker, and economist (1877–1970)
Dictating an account titled 'A Gift to Those Who Contemplate the Wonders of Cities,' this 14th-century Tangier-born traveler covered roughly 117,000 km — more than Marco Polo or Zheng He — who is he?
Ibn Battuta: Maghrebi traveller and scholar (1304–1368/1369)
In this Islamic narration, Muhammad makes a night journey and ascends to the sky, glimpsing the afterlife before returning — alluded to in Surah al-Isra. What is it called?
Signs of the coming of Judgement Day
Isra' and Mi'raj: Journey by Muhammad in Islamic tradition.

A follower of a controversial Bohemian religious reformer, this Czech military leader led Hussite forces to victory against three separate crusades and was never defeated in his military career — who is he?
A propertied peasant's daughter who said visions from Saint Margaret and Saint Catherine sent her to lift the siege of Orléans and crown Charles VII — which patron saint of France is this?
Joan of Arc: French folk heroine and saint (1412–1431)
Eldest son of a U.S. Attorney General and older brother of a future Health and Human Services secretary, this Massachusetts congressman founded a nonprofit heating-oil charity in 1979 — who is he?
Joseph P. Kennedy II: American businessman and politician (born 1952)

Also known as the Afrasiabids, this Turkic state ruled Central Asia from the 9th to the early 13th century, conquering Transoxiana and marking a shift from Iranic to Turkic dominance in the region — what was this state called?
Kara-Khanid Khanate: Turkic state in Central Asia from 840 to 1212.

Named by the prophet Mani as one of the four great powers of the 3rd century — alongside Persia, Rome, and China — this African realm was centered on a city in what's now Eritrea and northern Ethiopia. What was it?
Kingdom of Aksum: Polity in Africa and Arabia before 960.
As one of the youngest MPs ever elected to India's Lok Sabha in 1977, he went on to serve as Bihar's chief minister and later as the national railways minister — who is he?
Lalu Prasad Yadav: 20th chief minister of Bihar. Lalu was convicted in the Fodder Scam and was serving a term until 17 April 2021, when he was granted bail by the High Court.
Co-founder of a wrestling promotion that grew into a multinational company, this former Small Business Administration head became the 13th U.S. secretary of education in 2025 — who is she?
Linda McMahon: American administrator and business executive (born 1948)

Born in Atar in French West Africa and a veteran of the Western Sahara War against the Polisario Front, this military officer seized power in a bloodless coup and ruled Mauritania as president from 1984 to 2005 — who is he?
Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya: President of Mauritania from 1984 to 2005. Born in Atar, French West Africa, Ould Taya studied at Franco-Arab school and then French military school.
Sparked by a Japanese army claim that a soldier had gone missing near Beijing in July 1937, this three-day clash is considered the start of the Second Sino-Japanese War — what was it?
Marco Polo Bridge incident: Initial battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
This Florida congressman, a self-described libertarian populist and Trump ally, filed the 2023 motion that ousted Speaker Kevin McCarthy before resigning in 2024 — who is he?
Matt Gaetz: American politician and TV host (born 1982)
This legendary king of Phrygia was said to turn everything he touched into gold — who was he?
Midas: Phrygian royals, including mythical king with golden touch.
Born in 1950, this Indian activist has served since 2009 as the sixth Sarsanghchalak, or chief, of a major Hindu nationalist organization — who is he?

Serving as Japan's prime minister from 2010 to 2011, this politician was the first in years to hold the post for more than twelve months, and later published a memoir titled 'Fifty Years of Citizen Politics' — who is he?
Naoto Kan: Prime Minister of Japan from 2010 to 2011. On 26 August 2011, Kan announced his resignation.
A Filipino senator and journalist whose 1983 assassination helped topple Marcos and propelled his widow Corazon to the presidency — which opposition leader was he?
This April 1940 assault saw Nazi Germany occupy Denmark within hours and invade Norway on the same morning, launching the Norwegian Campaign — what was this codenamed?
Operation Weserübung: 1940 German invasion of Denmark and Norway in WWII.
Rising from aide-de-camp to Tsar Nicholas II to lieutenant general in World War I, this nobleman seized power in a 1918 coup to become hetman of a short-lived Ukrainian state — who is he?
Pavlo Skoropadsky: Ukrainian and Russian Cossack military and political official; Hetman of Ukraine (1918)
This Odawa war chief led Native Americans against the British in the Great Lakes region from 1763 to 1766, in a conflict that came to bear his name — who was he?
Pontiac (Odawa leader): 18th-century Native American war chief.

She served as France's Minister of Justice under Sarkozy before later becoming Minister of Culture across four different governments, and has been mayor of one of Paris's arrondissements since 2008. Who is this French politician?
Declared independent on a man-made platform in the Adriatic in 1968, this micronation used Esperanto as its official language before being demolished by Italian authorities — what was it called?
Republic of Rose Island: 1968 micronation in the Adriatic Sea. The Italian government viewed it as a ploy by Rosa to raise money from tourists while avoiding national taxation.
This U.S. Army officer led E Company's assault on the Belgian town of Foy after the siege of Bastogne was broken, and later served as the American governor of a Berlin prison — who is he?
Nominated by President George W. Bush in 2005, this jurist became just the second Italian American justice on the Supreme Court, after Antonin Scalia — who is he?
Samuel Alito: US Supreme Court justice since 2006.

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Lasting 872 days and killing an estimated 1.5 million from a prewar population of 3.2 million, this WWII blockade of the Soviet Union's second-largest city was never successfully captured — what was it?
Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.
A Thai Chinese general, he became the only king of Thonburi after leading the liberation of Siam from Burmese occupation and reuniting a country splintered among warlords — who was he?
Taksin: King of Siam from 1767 to 1782.
One of 24 Apollo astronauts to fly to the Moon, he commanded Apollo 10 and, with his crewmate, became the first to fly a Lunar Module in lunar orbit — which test pilot?
Thomas P. Stafford: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–2024)
Dubbed 'the Nelson of the East' by Western reporters, this Imperial Japanese Navy admiral penned Russia's fleet into Port Arthur before a decisive 1905 victory at Tsushima — who is he?

Raiding, trading, and settling from Scandinavia across Europe, North Africa, and even Newfoundland between the late 8th and 11th centuries, this seafaring people helped establish Kievan Rus'. Who were they?
Vikings: Norse seafarers, merchants and raiders.

The first conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, this 1805–1806 struggle pitted Napoleon's France against an alliance of Britain, Austria, Russia, Naples, Sicily, and Sweden, and included the Battle of Trafalgar — which conflict?
War of the Third Coalition: 1805–1806 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars. The Royal Navy, however, assured its naval dominance at the Battle of Trafalgar in October 1805.

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?
Dismembered by the Titans and reborn, this figure from Greek myth was sometimes identified with an Orphic version of Dionysus and linked by Aeschylus to Hades — who is he?
Zagreus: Figure in Greek mythology. In the earliest mention of Zagreus, he is paired with Gaia and called the "highest" god, though perhaps only in reference to the gods of the underworld.
Which one below was born first?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
TeX (published 1978) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Ernest Lawrence is a physicist. A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
Pick the chemist from these four.
What is the atomic number of Helium?
Helium: Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
In what year was B. R. Ambedkar born?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year was Plutonium discovered?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
In what year was Tungsten discovered?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
Ilyushin Il-96: Voronezh Aircraft Production Association. It is powered by four high-bypass Aviadvigatel PS-90 twin-spool turbofan engines.
In which country is Dassault Mirage 2000?
Dassault Mirage 2000: France. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
Who is credited with discovering Horologium?

Horologium (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.
Who is credited with discovering Hubble's law?
Hubble's law: Georges Lemaître. The Friedmann equations showed the universe might be expanding, and presented the expansion speed if that were the case.
Who is credited with discovering Eris?
Eris (dwarf planet): Michael E. Brown. Eris (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Hiding in coffee, fresh bread, and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is also what your liver makes when breaking down alcohol — and a prime culprit behind the morning-after hangover. What is it?
Acetaldehyde (IUPAC systematic name ethanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH3CH=O.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
This symptom, not a diagnosis by itself, refers to a loss of appetite in humans and — under the name 'inappetence' — in animals from dogs to goats. Which symptom?
Anorexia (symptom) is a medical term for a loss of appetite.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text from around 200 BC and named for a barberry-related plant genus, this yellow-pigmented alkaloid glows under ultraviolet light. What compound is it?
Berberine is an organic compound classified as benzylisoquinoline alkaloid.
Once known as the Russian Wolfhound until a 1936 name change, this elegant sighthound breed was historically used to hunt wolves — what breed is it?
Borzoi is a Russian breed of hunting dog of sighthound type.
Produced when quicklime is mixed with water, this white, powdery compound goes by many names in industry and food prep, where it's labeled E526 — what compound is it?
Calcium hydroxide (traditionally called slaked lime) is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Ca(OH)2.
Retired from Istanbul Technical University, this geologist holds foreign membership in both the US and Russian National Academies of Sciences. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör (born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.

This genus of flowering trees and shrubs, native to South and East Asia, Melanesia, and Australia, gave rise through extensive hybridization to oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and limes — what's the genus called?
Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the family Rutaceae.

What zoological term describes the internal-fertilization mating behavior in which a male animal introduces sperm directly into a female's reproductive tract — occurring via a 'cloacal kiss' in birds and most reptiles, or vaginally in mammals?
Copulation (zoology) is animal sexual behavior in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body, especially directly into the female's reproductive tract.
A staunch defender of Georg Cantor's set theory, this mathematician co-founded proof theory and became one of the most influential figures in his field — who is he?
David Hilbert (23 January 1862 - 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician and philosopher of mathematics and one of the most influential mathematicians of all time.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Noted for producing one of the most variable litter sizes of any dog breed, this active gun dog comes in 'field' and 'house' varieties and gave rise to its American cousin breed — what is it?
English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Confirming Maxwell's theoretical predictions, this 19th-century German physicist proved that electromagnetic waves actually exist — who is he?

Heinrich Hertz (hurts; 22 February 1857 - 1 January 1894) was a German physicist who first conclusively proved the existence of the electromagnetic waves proposed by James Clerk Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism.
This semi-synthetic opioid, often combined with acetaminophen or ibuprofen, treats severe pain and also suppresses cough — what drug is it?
Hydrocodone is a semi-synthetic opioid used to treat pain and as a cough suppressant.
Many plants stockpile this energy-storing polysaccharide in their roots instead of starch, and doctors still use it as the benchmark substance for testing kidney function — name the fiber?
Inulin are a group of naturally occurring polysaccharides produced by many types of plants, industrially most often extracted from chicory.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Alongside Robert Goddard and Hermann Oberth, this reclusive Russian scientist who lived in a log house near Kaluga is considered a founding father of modern rocketry — who is he?
Also called the great grey slug, this 10-20cm mollusc has a strange courtship where mating pairs suspend themselves in midair from a mucus thread — what species is it?
Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

Resembling some toxic look-alikes despite being a well-regarded edible, this basidiomycete fungus is a fairly common species on well-drained soils across temperate Eurasia, found solitary or in fairy rings in pastures — name the species?
Macrolepiota procera is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
First synthesized in 1982 near Darmstadt, this fleeting synthetic element of the periodic table's seventh period was named in 1997 after a pioneering Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist. What is it?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.

An Egyptian who studied architecture at Cairo University and worked as a civil engineer, this man was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta (September 1, 1968 - September 11, 2001) was an Egyptian engineer, architect, and the lead terrorist hijacker for al-Qaeda on American Airlines Flight 11.
This stocky Arctic whale carries a spiralled tusk up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to serve as weapon, tool, and sensor — what is it?
Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.

This cellular process, in which a cell's outer membrane engulfs a large particle to form an internal compartment, is a key immune-system mechanism for clearing pathogens and cellular debris — what is it called?

Phagocytosis (from Ancient Greek (phagein) 'to eat' and (kytos) 'cell') is the process by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to engulf a large particle (0.5 m), giving rise to an internal compartment called the phagosome.
This radioactive, silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 94 forms oxides in moist air that can expand a sample by up to 70% in volume — which element?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
This Eurasian fruit tree, also called the cherry plum, is believed to be one of the ancestral parents of the plum we cultivate today — what species is it?
Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum.
This biological process by which new organisms are produced from parents comes in two forms — one requiring a single organism, the other requiring two. What is it?
Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms - offspring - are produced from their parent or parents.

Originally conceived in the 1960s as a jet trainer before evolving into a supersonic strike aircraft, this joint British-French warplane — retired by both original operators — remains in service only with the Indian Air Force. Name it?
SEPECAT Jaguar is a British-French supersonic jet attack aircraft originally used by the British Royal Air Force and the French Air Force in the close air support and nuclear strike role.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
A single-seat, twin-engine, supermaneuverable 4.5-generation fighter derived from the Su-27, it was relabeled from "Su-27M" after the Soviet collapse to court export buyers — which Russian jet?
Sukhoi Su-35 (NATO reporting name: Flanker-E/M, occasionally nicknamed "Super Flanker") is the designation for two improved derivatives of the Su-27 air superiority fighter.
Enhanced by painted scenery and stagecraft like lighting, this live performing art shares its name with the very buildings where its shows are staged — what is it?

Theatre is a collaborative form of performing art that uses live performers, usually actors, to present experiences of a real or imagined event before a live audience in a specific place, often a stage.
Latin for 'three-headed,' this large muscle on the back of the upper arm has three parts, one of which also crosses the shoulder joint — name the muscle?
Triceps (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.

Native to Europe and parts of Asia, this parasitic plant draws water and nutrients from host trees and has long featured in European mythology, now commonly used in Christmas decorations — what is it?
Viscum album is a species of mistletoe in the family Santalaceae, commonly called European mistletoe, common mistletoe, or simply mistletoe (Old English mistle).
This mosquito-borne viral disease causes chills, nausea, and muscle pain, and in about 15% of cases progresses to liver damage that turns the skin a telltale color — what disease is it?
Yellow fever is a viral disease of typically short duration.
This class of bony fish accounts for nearly 99% of all living fish species, ranging in size from an 8-millimeter minnow to a giant sunfish weighing 2,700 kilograms — what is it?
Actinopterygii: Class of ray-finned bony fishes.
Its very name comes from the Arabic for 'the kohl,' and chemically it's any compound carrying a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon — a family that ranges from methanol to cholesterol. What is it?
Alcohol (chemistry): Organic compound with at least one hydroxyl (–OH) group.
This functional group, formed by replacing a carboxylic acid's hydroxyl with an amino group, creates the peptide bonds that link amino acids into proteins — what is it?
Amide: Organic compounds of the form RC(=O)NR′R″.
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Ranging from a racing tachycardia to a sluggish bradycardia, this catch-all term covers any heartbeat that strays from normal sinus rhythm — what is it called?
Arrhythmia: Group of medical conditions characterized by irregular heartbeat.
This Mexican mole salamander never grows up — it reaches sexual maturity while staying fully aquatic with feathery external gills, skipping metamorphosis entirely. What is it?
Axolotl: Species of salamander. The axolotl (from Classical Nahuatl: āxōlōtl [aːˈʃoːloːtɬ]; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.
A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid hiding in petroleum, this ring-shaped hydrocarbon helps give gasoline its distinctive aroma — what is it?
Despite being just 12 to 20 cm long, this small marine creature's vivid markings flash brighter when it feels threatened, and its bite delivers a neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Blue-ringed octopus: Four species of mollusk.

This tropical tree's moderately ripe flesh, once cooked, is said to taste like a fresh-baked loaf with a potato-like flavor, and 18th-century navigators carried it in seedless form to the Caribbean — what is it?
Breadfruit: Edible fruit-bearing tree in family. Moraceae.
The fifth most abundant element in Earth's crust and a reactive alkaline earth metal, this element's name comes from the Latin word for 'lime' obtained by heating limestone — what is it?
Calcium: Chemical element with atomic number 20 (Ca)
This compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into a cell's mitochondria to be burned for energy and is naturally concentrated in muscles like the heart — what is it?
Carnitine: Compound active in mitochondria. Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
In calculus, this formula computes the derivative of a composite function by multiplying together the derivatives of its two component functions — what is it called?

Native to Sri Lanka, the inner bark of this evergreen tree is the original source of a beloved baking spice, sometimes distinguished from a cheaper cousin as the 'true' or 'Ceylon' variety — which tree?
Cinnamomum verum: Species of tree. The inner bark of the tree is historically regarded as the spice cinnamon, though this term was later generalized to include C. cassia as well.
Also known as foremilk or historically as 'beestings,' this early substance produced by mammary glands right after birth delivers antibodies and immune factors to newborns. What is it?
Colostrum: Form of milk produced immediately following the delivery of newborn.
Its round nuts distinguish it from the longer filbert, and its coppiced wood once built wattle-and-daub walls across England — which shrub?
Corylus avellana: Species of tree (common hazel)
Two polynucleotide chains coil around each other into a double helix to carry the genetic instructions of nearly every living thing — what is this macromolecule?
DNA: Molecule that carries genetic information.
Sold under the brand name Valium, this benzodiazepine anxiolytic treats anxiety, seizures, alcohol withdrawal, and muscle spasms — and can even induce memory loss during procedures; what is it?
Diazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Diazepam, sold under the brand name Valium among others, is a medication of the benzodiazepine family that acts as an anxiolytic.
The only living relative of the extinct Steller's sea cow, this seagrass-grazing marine mammal is most abundant in the waters of northern Australia — what is it?
Dugong: Species of marine mammal. It is one of four living species of the order Sirenia, which also includes three species of manatees.
Co-founding Mattel with his wife Ruth, this inventor helped bring Barbie, Hot Wheels, and Chatty Cathy to toy shelves — who is he?
Elliot Handler: American inventor and business magnate (1916–2011)
Made by yeast fermenting sugars and once used as a general anesthetic, this colorless flammable liquid is the world's second most consumed drug, behind only caffeine — what is it?
Proposed in 1724 by a physicist who set water's freezing point at 32 degrees and boiling at 212, this temperature scale was originally anchored to a freezing brine solution — which scale?
Fahrenheit: Temperature scale. The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale based on one proposed in 1724 by the physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit (1686–1736).
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?

After dropping out of Harvard to help build early versions of Windows at Microsoft, this developer co-founded a studio that made Half-Life and later launched a digital storefront called Steam — who is he?
Known only from teeth and four jawbones, this extinct genus of giant ape roamed China for nearly two million years and is now thought to be a close relative of the orangutan — what is it?
Gigantopithecus: Extinct genus of primate. The species may have been sexually dimorphic, with males much bigger than females.

Native from Mexico down to southern Brazil, this large arboreal lizard can grow past six feet long, is a popular but demanding pet, and has become invasive in many warm regions worldwide — which species?
Green iguana: Species of reptile. Usually, this animal is simply called the iguana.

Named after a bird of prey, this British-developed attack aircraft was the only truly successful vertical-takeoff design of its era, able to fly from car parks and forest clearings instead of vulnerable airbases — which aircraft?
Harrier jump jet: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace.

A Greek physician and philosopher of the classical era, this figure is hailed as the "Father of Medicine" for championing prognosis, clinical observation, and the now-discredited theory of bodily humors — who is he?
Hippocrates: Ancient Greek physician (c. 460 – c. 370 BCE)
Though phylogenetically closer to cats, these African carnivores resemble dogs thanks to convergent evolution, and their family has just four living species — what animal is it?
Symbolized by the '∞' sign and debated by philosophers since ancient Greece, this endless concept was later shown by Georg Cantor to come in different sizes when applied to sets. What is it?
Infinity: Mathematical concept. Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This neo-Keynesian economist gave his name to a model for censored data — the 'tobit' — while advising the Fed and championing government action against recessions; who is he?
James Tobin: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2002)
While tinkering with electromagnets, this American physicist discovered self-inductance and went on to become the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution — who was he?
Joseph Henry: American physicist and inventor (1797–1878)
The largest joint in the human body, it's a modified hinge that links the thigh to the lower leg via two separate joints — what is it?
Knee: Leg joint in primates. The knee is a modified hinge joint, which permits flexion and extension as well as slight internal and external rotation.
Called a 'universal genius,' this Swiss polymath founded graph theory and topology while introducing much of modern mathematical notation — who is he?
The third wide-body airliner to enter service after the 747 and DC-10, this trijet used an S-duct to route its third engine through the tail — which aircraft?

Lockheed L-1011 TriStar: American wide-body trijet airliner. The Lockheed L-1011 TriStar (pronounced "El-ten-eleven") is an American medium-to-long-range, wide-body trijet airliner built by the Lockheed Corporation.
A chemical engineer and physician who also served in the Peace Corps, she became the first African-American woman in space aboard Endeavour in 1992 — who is she?
Mae Jemison: American astronaut, doctor and engineer (born 1956)

This field studies abstract things like numbers, shapes, sets and probabilities, using logical proof to establish truths it calls theorems — and its branches include algebra, geometry and number theory. What is it?
Mathematics: Field of knowledge. Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
Sold under the brand Glucophage, this first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes is favored partly because it isn't associated with weight gain. What drug is it?
Metformin: Medication used to treat diabetes.
Medically termed a 'spontaneous abortion,' this is the loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently — distinct from a stillbirth, which occurs after 20 weeks. What is it?
Miscarriage: Natural premature termination of pregnancy.
Native to the Americas from Texas down to Argentina, this domesticated waterfowl species has also gone feral in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe — which species?
Muscovy duck: Species of bird. The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.
A cable-like bundle of axons wrapped in three layers of connective tissue, this structure carries electrochemical signals called action potentials — what is it?
Nerve: Cable-like bundle of axons. The axons are bundled together into groups called fascicles, and each fascicle is wrapped in a layer of connective tissue called the perineurium.

This healthcare profession blends the art and science of caring, focusing on protecting and promoting health, preventing illness, and easing suffering through compassionate, hands-on care — what field is it?
Nursing: Health care profession. Nurses may help coordinate care performed by other providers or act independently as nursing professionals.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
Usually caused by a virus but sometimes by strep bacteria, this inflammation of the back of the throat brings on a sore throat, fever, and sometimes a hoarse voice — what is it called?
Pharyngitis: Inflammation of the back of the throat. Pharyngitis is a type of upper respiratory tract infection.
Connected to the fetus by the umbilical cord, this temporary organ handles nutrient and waste exchange between mother and baby during pregnancy — what is it?
Placenta: Organ that connects the fetus to the uterine wall.
Despite its common name, this burrowing rodent native to North American grasslands is actually a type of ground squirrel, not a canine — what is it?
Prairie dog: Genus of ground squirrels.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.

Numbering more than 9,000 species, these tiny hexapods are no longer classified as true insects and get their scientific class name from Greek words meaning 'glue' and 'peg,' after a structure called the collophore — what are they called?
Known in antiquity as 'oil of vitriol,' this odorless, syrupy liquid is so thirsty for water that it never occurs pure in nature and will char nearly anything it touches — which substance is it?
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Named for its three heads — medial, lateral, and long — which upper-arm muscle straightens the elbow when it contracts?
Triceps: Muscle on the back of the upper arm. The triceps, or triceps brachii (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
Developed for chemical warfare after research into pesticide toxicity, this oily amber liquid is lethal in just tens of milligrams and is more potent than sarin — what is this compound?
VX (nerve agent): VX is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
Also called Japanese horseradish, this pungent rhizome is ground into a paste for sushi and has been recorded as a food since the 8th century — what is it?

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.
What is the chemical symbol for lithium?
The symbol for lithium is Li. Lithium is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Which of these is a comedian?
Louis de Funès is a comedian. Louis Germain David de Funès de Galarza (French: [lwi d(ə) fynɛs]; 31 July 1914 – 27 January 1983) was a French actor and comedian.
In what year was Matt Rife born?
Matt Rife: Matthew Steven Rife (born September 10, 1995) is an American comedian and actor.
In what year was Colin Firth born?
Colin Firth: Colin Andrew Firth (born 10 September 1960) is an English actor and producer.
In what year was Natalie Wood born?
Natalie Wood (née Zacharenko; July 20, 1938 – November 29, 1981) was an American actress.
In what year was Jim Caviezel born?
Jim Caviezel: James Patrick Caviezel Jr. ( kə-VEE-zəl; born September 26, 1968) is an American actor.
